item.subject: science
item.chapter_label: Earth, Sun and the apparent motion of the sky
item.stem: Meera notes that the group of stars she sees from her Chennai terrace at 9 p.m. in January is different from the group she sees at 9 p.m. in July. Her teacher asks the class to explain why. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The stars move around the Earth once every 24 hours, so different stars appear.
options.B: Earth revolves around the Sun, so at the same time of night we face a different part of space at different times of the year.
options.C: Earth stops rotating on its axis for part of the year, so the sky changes.
options.D: The Sun moves to the other side of the sky at night, hiding some stars.
